items.title: Section: The Eight Fulfilling-Requests Patiences — Three Endured From Others, Five Chosen for Their Sake

items.zh: 云何菩薩遂求忍？當知此忍略有八種。謂諸菩薩，於諸有苦來求索者惡逼能忍。於極凶暴上品惡業諸有情所，依法大悲不損惱忍。於諸出家犯戒者所，依法大悲不損惱忍。復有五種耐勤苦忍。謂能堪耐除遣有苦有情眾苦所有勤苦。又能堪耐求法勤苦，又能堪耐法隨法行所有勤苦，又能堪耐即於彼法廣為他說所有勤苦。又能堪耐於諸有情所為、所作正與助伴所有勤苦。如是八種，名遂求忍。若於有情有損惱者，由忍故離。若於有情是所求者，由忍故與；是故說此名遂求忍。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's fulfilling-requests patience? One should know this patience is, in brief, of eight kinds. Bodhisattvas who are able to endure the hostile pressure of suffering beings who come demanding something. Bodhisattvas who, towards beings of extremely violent and grievous karma, rely on genuine dharma-grounded great compassion and remain patient without any resulting harm to those beings. Bodhisattvas who, towards ordained persons who have broken the precepts, likewise rely on genuine dharma-grounded great compassion and remain patient without harming them. There are, further, five kinds of patience enduring diligent exertion: enduring the exertion of working to relieve suffering beings of their suffering; enduring the exertion of seeking the teaching; enduring the exertion of actually practising the teaching once received; enduring the exertion of broadly teaching that same teaching to others; and enduring the exertion of genuinely lending a hand in whatever beings are working to accomplish. These eight together are called fulfilling-requests patience. Where harming beings might seem called for, patience keeps the bodhisattva from it; whatever the bodhisattva seeks on beings' behalf, patience is what brings it about — and it is for this reason that this is called fulfilling-requests patience.

items.title: Section: The Nine Both-Worlds-Happiness Patiences — Cold, Heat, Hunger, Thirst, Insects, Wind, Snakes, and Fatigue

items.zh: 云何菩薩此世他世樂忍？當知此忍略有九種。謂諸菩薩住不放逸，於諸善法悉能堪忍；於諸寒熱悉能堪忍；於諸飢渴悉能堪忍；於蚊虻觸悉能堪忍；於諸風日悉能堪忍；於蛇蠍觸悉能堪忍；於諸劬勞所生種種若身、若心疲惓憂惱悉能堪忍；於墮生死、生老病死等苦有情，現前哀愍而修行忍。如是菩薩修行忍故，能令自身於現法中得安樂住，不為一切惡不善法之所陵雜；能引後世安樂因緣；亦能令他修行種種現法後法安樂正行。是名此世他世樂忍。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's patience of happiness in this world and the next? One should know this patience is, in brief, of nine kinds. Bodhisattvas, abiding without carelessness, are fully able to endure whatever hardship arises in the practice of wholesome dharmas; are fully able to endure cold and heat; are fully able to endure hunger and thirst; are fully able to endure the bite of mosquitoes and horseflies; are fully able to endure wind and sun; are fully able to endure the sting of snakes and scorpions; are fully able to endure whatever bodily fatigue and distress arises from sustained exertion; are fully able to endure whatever mental fatigue and distress arises from it; and, towards beings caught in birth, ageing, sickness, death, and every other suffering of saṃsāra, meet them with genuine, present compassion, and in this way practice patience. Bodhisattvas who practice patience in this way are able to dwell in genuine ease in this present life, never overrun by any unwholesome affliction; are able to bring about the causes of ease in lives to come; and are able, moreover, to lead others to practise the same genuinely beneficial conduct, in this life and the next. This is called the patience of happiness in this world and the next.

items.title: Section: The Ten Purity Patiences Close the Entire Chapter on the Perfection of Patience

items.zh: 云何菩薩清淨忍？當知此忍略有十種。謂諸菩薩遇他所作不饒益事、損惱違越，終不返報；亦不意憤；亦無怨嫌意樂相續；恒常現前，欲作饒益，先後無異，非一益己捨而不益；於有怨者自往悔謝；終不令他生疲厭已，然後受謝，恐其疲厭，纔謝便受；於不堪忍，成就增上猛利慚愧；依於堪忍，於大師所，成就增上猛利愛敬；依不損惱諸有情故，於諸有情，成就猛利哀愍愛樂；一切不忍并助伴法皆得斷故，離欲界欲。由此十相，當知菩薩所修行忍清淨無垢。當知此中，初自性忍，廣說乃至後清淨忍，如是能生廣博無量大菩提果。忍為依止，是諸菩薩能圓滿忍波羅蜜多，能證無上正等菩提。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's purity patience? One should know this patience is, in brief, of ten kinds. Bodhisattvas who, meeting harmful, injurious, or offensive acts committed by others, never retaliate; who feel no inward resentment at all; who harbour no lingering grudge or resentment continuing on afterwards; who constantly, presently wish to benefit that very being, with no difference before and after — never helping once and then abandoning further help; who, towards anyone they have wronged, go personally to apologise; who never let another person exhaust themselves pleading before finally accepting their apology, but instead, fearing exactly that exhaustion, accept the apology the moment it is offered; who, when their own apology is refused, feel genuine and forceful shame; who, grounded in this very capacity for patience, hold genuine and forceful reverence towards the Great Teacher, the Buddha; who, grounded in never wishing harm on any being, hold genuine and forceful compassion and affection towards all beings; and who have entirely severed every form of intolerance together with its accompanying afflictions, thereby becoming free of the desire-realm's own bondage. By these ten marks, one should understand a bodhisattva's practice of patience to be genuinely pure and free of any defiling taint. One should understand that all of this — from the very first, the patience of intrinsic nature, in full detail down to this final purity patience — gives rise to a vast and immeasurable fruit of supreme awakening. Relying on patience as its foundation, bodhisattvas are able to fulfil the perfection of patience, and are able to realise supreme, complete awakening.

items.title: Section: The Perfection of Diligence Opens — the Eyes, Ears, and Hands of a Truly Diligent Life

items.zh: 云何菩薩精進波羅蜜多？嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，名略說精進。謂九種相精進，名為菩薩精進波羅蜜多。一者、自性精進，二者、一切精進，三者、難行精進，四者、一切門精進，五者、善士精進，六者、一切種精進，七者、遂求精進，八者、此世他世樂精進，九者、清淨精進。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter twelve: diligence. What is a bodhisattva's perfection of diligence? A summary verse states: "Intrinsic nature, comprehensive scope, difficult practice; comprehensive gateways, virtuous persons; comprehensive kinds, fulfilling requests; both-worlds happiness, purity — these nine kinds of mark are, in brief, called diligence." These nine marks of diligence together constitute a bodhisattva's perfection of diligence: first, the diligence of intrinsic nature; second, comprehensive diligence; third, the diligence of difficult practice; fourth, comprehensive-gateway diligence; fifth, virtuous-person diligence; sixth, comprehensive-kind diligence; seventh, fulfilling-requests diligence; eighth, the diligence of happiness in this world and the next; ninth, purity diligence.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Diligence — a Courageous Aspiration, Carried Through Into Real Action

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性精進？謂諸菩薩其心勇悍，堪能攝受無量善法，利益安樂一切有情，熾然無間，無有顛倒，及此所起身語意動，當知是名菩薩所行精進自性。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's diligence of intrinsic nature? Bodhisattvas whose minds are genuinely courageous and resolute, capable of taking up limitless wholesome practices and of genuinely benefiting and bringing ease to every being, sustaining this blazingly and without interruption, entirely free of distortion — together with the bodily, verbal, and mental action that arises from this — should be understood as constituting a bodhisattva's own intrinsic nature of diligence.

blocks.text: The last aspects of patience, then the perfection of **diligence** (vīrya) begins.
Eight kinds: three endured from others' pressure, five chosen for their sake. Venerable Miào Jìng: compassion here follows wisdom, not mere emotion.
Enduring "cold, heat, hunger, thirst, mosquitoes and gnats, wind and sun, snakes and scorpions", and bodily and mental fatigue from effort. Master Cháng Bǎi: the English merges the last two.

Ten marks, including: "towards one who bears a grudge, they go and apologise themselves; they never make the other weary before accepting an apology". Venerable Miào Jìng: one's preceptor is the "lesser teacher", the Buddha the Great Teacher.
"These nine marks constitute the perfection of diligence." The names are the same as before.

"Minds genuinely courageous and resolute, capable of taking up limitless wholesome practices and benefiting beings", and acting on it in body, speech, and mind. Master Cháng Bǎi tells of a monk whose legs a robber broke, who by dawn had attained arhatship, reflecting: "this day has passed; life diminishes, like fish in shrinking water." Venerable Miào Jìng: first solve the problems of livelihood (ease), then of thought (benefit).

quiz.q: The fulfilling-requests patience closes "for what is sought, through patience one gives." How do the lectures explain "suì qiú" here?
options: Cháng Bǎi: satisfying one's own inner aim — the first three concern beings' pressure, the last five the bodhisattva's active benefit; Miào Jìng: fulfilling what the other seeks
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "suì" is satisfying one's own inner aim; the first three concern patience under beings' pressure, the last five the bodhisattva's effort in actively benefiting beings. Venerable Miào Jìng: fulfilling what the other hopes for. The English leans towards "what beings seek."

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain the "dharma-grounded great compassion" in this patience?
options: "dharma" is the perfection of wisdom — great compassion arising from wisdom, not from emotion
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "dharma" is the perfection of wisdom — great compassion following wisdom, not emotional compassion. Master Cháng Bǎi: great compassion containing wisdom, not superficial compassion of craving and views.

quiz.q: Two-world patience has nine kinds, but the English merges bodily and mental fatigue. How does Master Cháng Bǎi count nine?
options: splitting "bodily and mental fatigue and distress" into the seventh and eighth
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the seventh is enduring bodily fatigue and the eighth mental fatigue from exertion. The English merges them, yielding only eight.

quiz.q: Among the ten marks of pure patience, what about those who bear grudges and apologies?
options: going oneself to apologise to those with grudges; accepting another's apology immediately without making them weary
quiz.why: "Towards one who bears a grudge, they go and apologise themselves; they never make the other weary before accepting an apology — fearing their weariness, they accept as soon as it is offered." Venerable Miào Jìng illustrates the difficulty of consistency: "I won't retaliate for three days — after that, maybe trouble."

quiz.q: The English renders "dà shī" as "their teacher." How do the lectures explain it?
options: the Great Teacher is the Buddha; one's preceptor is the "lesser teacher"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: besides the Great Teacher there is a lesser teacher — your preceptor; the Buddha is the Great Teacher. Master Cháng Bǎi likewise: the Great Teacher (the Buddha). The English "their teacher" is imprecise.

quiz.q: How is the perfection of diligence explained?
options: the same nine aspects: intrinsic nature … purity
quiz.why: "These nine marks of diligence constitute a bodhisattva's perfection of diligence." Venerable Miào Jìng: the names are the same as for giving, discipline, and patience, but the meanings inside differ.

quiz.q: "Benefiting and bringing ease to all beings" — how does Venerable Miào Jìng order ease and benefit?
options: first solve material problems (ease), then problems of thinking (benefit)
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: first solve problems of livelihood — that is ease; then solve problems of thinking — that is benefit. "Blazing" means vigorous.
